2. In a nutshell, the accusations against the accused and the background scenario so far as relevant for the disposal of this application are as follows:
2.1

On 18.12.2024, a complaint was lodged by the applicant- original complainant alleging that when he was going to the agricultural field of one Vikrambhai Prajapati which was taken on lease by him for the purpose of sowing wheat along with his younger brother Rajubhai Sagrambhai Meer, and as the said agricultural field of Vikrambhai Prajapati is situated near the Hanumanji Temple of his village, he decided to go there from passing through one agricultural field situated at the edge of the road opposite Hanumanji temple, and when he was passing through the said field, at that time, one Virambhai Gandhubhai Bodiya (Bharwad) came from behind on his motorcycle and stopped our tractor, and told me that how dare you to pass from our agricultural field, and by saying so, he started hurling abuses to me, upon which, I told him not to use such kind of filthy language, and then proceeded towards the agricultural field of Vikrambhai Prajapati.

Thereafter, he phoned his uncle Ghanshyambhai Kadvabhai Meer and informed him about the said incident, and when he reached to the agricultural field of Vikrambhai Prajapati at around quarter to three, and at that time, one Virambhai Gandhubhai Bodiya from our village came there along with Vijaybhai Bhopabhai @ Ranchhodbhai Bodiya on a motorcycle, and at that time,
Virambhai was having a axe in his hand, and Vijaybhai Bhopabhai @ Ranchhodbhai NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined

Bodiya was having a wooden stick in his hand, and one Mahesbhai Viththalbhai Bodiya also came there running with the wooden stick in his hand, and came to me, and started abusing me and my brother, and told that now they will finish them, and by saying so, Virambhai Gandhubhai Bodiya, with an intention to kill me, tried to hit a blow with the axe in his hand on my head, however, as I raised my right hand in rescue, the said axe was hit on his palm near the thumb, and

then the persons accompanied Virambhai, namely, Vijaybhai Bhopabhai @ Ranchhodbhai Bodiya and Maheshbhai Viththalbhai Bodiya, started giving stick blows to me indiscriminately, due to which, my brother Rajubhai also intervened to save me, and during that time, I also called my uncles Virambhai Khodabhai Meer and told him that Vikrambhai Ghandhubhai Bodiya and his accomplices will kill us and told him to save us, and therefore, my uncle Virambhai Khodabhai and Khodabhai Bhikhabhai and Sodabhai Bhikhabhai and other family members came there and saved us from three of them, and while leaving, all the three accused persons also gave threats of dire consequences to me, and when we were shifted to Primary Health Center for treatment, there I came to know that upon receiving information from me about the abuses given by Virambhai Ghandhubhai to us, my uncle, namely,
Ghanshayambhai went to the house of Virambhai Ghandhubhai to confront him, however,

Having given a fair idea as regards the case of the prosecution, I may now narrate few events so far as the respondents accused are concerned.
2.3 After the registration of the FIR, the respondents-accused came to be arrested and sent to the judicial custody.

2.4 Therefore, they first preferred regular bail application before charge-sheet before the Sessions Court at Dhodka being Criminal Misc. Application No.494 of 2024 on 31.12.2024, which was strongly opposed by the complainant by filing objections on 03.01.2025 as also by the investigating officer by filing an affidavit dated 03.01.2025.

2.5 Thereafter, vide the impugned order dated 07.01.2025, the respondents-accused were enlarged on regular bail by the 10th Addl. Sessions Judge, Dhodka, Ahmedabad (Rural), being aggrieved with which, the original complainant is here before this Court with the present application, seeking cancellation of bail.
3. Learned advocate Ms. Kanan A. Odedra appearing for the original complainant, submitted that the bail granted to the respondents-accused deserves to be cancelled.

She submitted that the Sessions Judge ought not to have exercised his discretion solely on the ground that the injuries received by the complainant and his uncle was simple in nature and that they were discharged from the hospital, but the learned Judge also, while considering the bail application, ought to have taken into consideration the intention or the mens rea of the accused NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined persons at the time of committing the offence.
It was not the scuffle that ensued all of a sudden at the spur of the moment, but it was a premeditated attack with the deadly weapons upon the complainant and the injured witness.

She further submitted that the impugned order passed by the Sessions Judge reflects total non-application of mind, as how the learned Sessions Judge took it so casually that the complainant received simple injuries on his thumb only, when it was the clear cut case of the complainant that the accused tried to give the blow on his head with the axe to kill him, but as he raised his hand to save himself, he sustained injury on his hand which required 19 stitches, and thereby completely brushed aside the aspect of mens rea on the part of the accused of killing the complainant.
Moreover, the accused are influential persons holding significant social, political or economic power, which raises a serious concerned about the safety of the applicant and his family.

She also submitted that the learned Sessions Judge has also ignored the aspect of the presence of the respondents-accused at the field of the applicant with deadly weapons in their hands, and an evidence in the form of video and photo is also there in the possession of the applicant, showing the respondents-accused in the field of the applicant with the deadly weapons.
She submitted that the impugned order of bail is almost like a judgment of acquittal ignoring relevant aspects and principles as regards grant of bail in an offence of attempt to murder.

Thus, it has been submitted Mahipatbhai Sagrambhai Mer vs State Of Gujarat on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161854608/

Heard the learned advocate appearing for the applicant and the learned APP, as also perused the record.

5. The case on hand pertains to cancellation of bail granted to the accused, and according to me, in an application for cancellation of bail, the conduct subsequent to release on bail and the supervening circumstances are the relevant factors to be kept in mind while deciding the cancellation of bail application.

It is no doubt true that the error being committed by the learned trial judge as well as the non-consideration of relevant aspects while setting the accused at liberty are also the relevant factors to be borne in mind at the time of deciding cancellation of bail application, still the same do not have much significance, on the basis of which, the order granting bail to the accused can be reversed, as it may be taken into consideration and determined during the course of trial.

The consideration of cancellation of bail is different from the consideration for grant of bail, and the bail can be cancelled only on existence of cogent and overwhelming circumstances, but not on re- appreciation of the facts of the case.
It is a settled law that cancellation of bail should not be by way of punishment even if prima facie case against the accused is established.

6. I have also gone through the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge, and it appears from the same that all the relevant aspects germane to the grant of bail have been considered by the Sessions Judge and, therefore, the discretion exercised could not be said to be perverse or illegal in any manner.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined 7.
I have also gone through the averments made in the application.

It appears from the same that,
the cancellation is sought for on the ground that some relevant aspects were not taken into consideration by the learned trial judge while enlarging the accused on bail.
It is the case of the complainant that he was being brutally assaulted by the respondents- accused, and their intention was to kill him while opposing the bail application before the trial court.

However, it appears from the impugned judgment that neither the learned advocate for the complainant nor the investigating officer had brought on record any concrete evidence with regard to the mens rea on the part of the accused persons that their intention was to kill him, and even otherwise if they are heavily harping upon the said aspect, then still the doors are not closed for the prosecution to establish the said aspect as the trial is still underway.
8. Here, in the case at hand, it is not the case of the complainant that the respondents-accused has breached any of the conditions imposed upon him by the trial court while being released on bail.

The respondents-accused are at liberty since January, 2025, i.e. for more than five months, and during this period, not a single incident of non-compliance of the order passed by the trial court is reported against the respondents-accused, or brought on record before this Court.

Hence, solely on the ground that some relevant aspects were claimed to have been not taken into consideration by the Mahipatbhai Sagrambhai Mer vs State Of Gujarat on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161854608/
4 trial court, the entire order of granting bail to the respondents- accused cannot be vitiated.

Moreover, while considering degree of burden of prove lie upon prosecution or complainant/Informant, when an application for cancellation of bail moved, is not to the extent of proving by a mathematical certainty or beyond reasonable doubt but it must establish its case by showing on a preponderance of probabilities that accused has attempted or may attempt to or tamper or has tampered with witnesses.
It may also be proved by test of balance of probabilities that accused has abused his liberty or it may show that there is reasonable apprehension that he will interfere with course of justice.
This Court approved Bombay High Court decision in Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain 60

entities.text: Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bombay
Law Reporter

465 that test adopted by the Court would be, whether material placed before it is such as to lead to the conclusion that there is a strong prima facie case that accused if allowed to be at large he would tamper with prosecution witnesses and impede course of justice.
Mere unfounded apprehension or self imagined threat by prosecution or Informant-Complainant would not justify cancellation of bail, granted to accused.

10. In Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481, the Court held that grounds for cancellation of bail under Sections 437(5) and 439(2) are identical, namely, bail granted under Section 437(1) or (2) or Section 439(1) can be cancelled where (i) accused misuses his liberty by indulging in similar criminal activity, (ii) interferes with the course of investigation, (iii) attempts to tamper with evidence or witnesses, (iv) threatens witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined smooth investigation, (v) there is likelihood of his fleeing to another country, (vi) attempts to make himself scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency, (vii) attempts to place himself beyond the reach of his surety, etc.
11.

entities.text: Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also held that above grounds are illustrative and not exhaustive.
Rejection of bail stands on one footing but cancellation of bail is a harsh order since it interferes with liberty of individual and must not be lightly resorted to.

12 In Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349, the Court held that rejection of bail in a non-bailable case at initial stage and cancellation of bail so granted, has to be dealt with and considered on different basis.

entities.text: Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing cancellation of bail, already granted.

Court further said that generally speaking grounds of cancellation of bail, broadly i.e. illustrative and not exhaustive are : (i) interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice; (ii) evasion or attempt to evade due course of justice;
(iii) abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner; (iv) Satisfaction of Court, on the basis of material placed on record of possibility of accused absconding.

5 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Court also reminded that bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying concession of bail during trial.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined 14.

In CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296, in para 23,
Court said :
"....that there is difference between yardstick for cancellation of bail and appeal against the order granting bail.

entities.text: CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of bail already granted.

Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail are, interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concessions granted to the accused in any manner.
These are all only few illustrative materials.
The satisfaction of the Court on the basis of the materials placed on record of the possibility of the accused absconding is another reason justifying the cancellation of bail.

In other words, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial."

15. Position, influence and resources of accused have also been held relevant factors to adjudge whether accused is likely to interfere with administration of justice, trial or tamper with witness or evidence.

16. Considerations and relevant aspects by a Court while granting a bail are different than those when an application for cancellation of bail has come up before the Court and this aspect has been considered by a three-Judges Bench of Supreme Court in State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411 wherein the Bench had an occasion to consider an order dated 11.04.1978 passed by Delhi High NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined Court rejecting Delhi Administration's application for cancellation of bail of respondent Sanjay Gandhi.

entities.text: State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court observed that rejection of bail, when bail applied is one thing;
cancellation of bail already granted is quite another.
It is easier to reject a bail application in a non-bailable case than to cancel a bail granted in such a case.

Cancellation of bail necessarily involves review of a decision already made and can, by and large, be permitted only, if, by reason of supervening circumstances, it would be no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow accused to retain his freedom during the trial.
17. In X vs. The State of Telangana and Ors.

entities.text: X vs. The State of Telangana and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2018)16 SCC 511, accused, a Film Producer, based in Mumbai, was charged of offences under Sections 376, 342, 493, 506, 354(C) of IPC.
Accused got anticipatory bail from Sessions Judge on 13.01.2017 and had advantage of that order for about eight months.

The said order was cancelled by Sessions Judge on the ground that accused has not Mahipatbhai Sagrambhai Mer vs State Of Gujarat on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161854608/
6 disclosed that he was also accused in 2G Spectrum case.

entities.text: Mahipatbhai Sagrambhai Mer vs State Of Gujarat on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This cancellation order was affirmed by High Court and also by Supreme Court.
Thereafter accused moved a bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C., which was allowed by High Court and accused was released on bail.
This order was challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
Upholding the said order, Court said that bail once granted should not be cancelled unless a cogent case, based on supervening event has been made out.
18. In Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors.

entities.text: Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2018) 16 SCC 10 bail granted to accused by High Court in the case registered under Sections 498-A, 302, 120-B IPC was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1421/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2025 undefined challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
The Court noticed that accused-2's bail application was rejected by Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ghaziabad and thereafter bail was granted by High Court.
The Court said that gravity of offence is a relevant factor but not the sole ground to deny bail if there are other overwhelming circumstances justifying grant of bail.
Noticing special feature, Court upheld order of High Court granting bail.

19. Thus, the broad principles, which are to be considered by this Court while granting bail and when bail is already granted but an application for cancellation has come up for consideration, as discussed above, show that there is no thumb rule in both the situations.

However, it is true that factors relevant for grant of bail are different and approach required to be adopted while considering application for cancellation of bail is different.
20.

Looking to above exposition of law as also the fact and circumstances of the case, I find that there is no material available on record to show any justification for cancellation of bail after more than five months and, therefore, order of cancellation of bail cannot be justified at this stage.
21.
In the result, the present application fails and is hereby rejected.

(DIVYESH A. JOSHI,J) VAHID Mahipatbhai Sagrambhai Mer vs State Of Gujarat on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161854608/
